title: Kafka vs Kinesis: Which Scales Better? ⚡
fb_caption:
Apache Kafka vs Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

• Throughput: Kafka excels with raw, high-volume throughput, while Kinesis offers managed scalability with potential for higher latency.
• Latency: Kafka generally offers lower end-to-end latency for real-time processing.
• Consistency: Kafka provides stronger ordering guarantees and durability (at-least-once, exactly-once).
• Failure Modes: Kafka's distributed nature demands careful operational management; Kinesis is managed by AWS, simplifying ops but with vendor lock-in.
• Operational Overhead: Kafka requires significant self-management; Kinesis is fully managed, reducing operational burden.

Recommendation: For maximum control, raw performance, and lower latency with self-managed infrastructure, choose Kafka. For ease of use, managed scalability, and seamless AWS integration, Kinesis is a strong contender.
